content.content:
---
name: plar
description: Map a project's code, UI states and references to pixel-art asset requirements; create or update plar.txt and hand a selected asset to PIXL for production.
---

PLAR (Pixel Lab Asset Requirements) turns project context into a usable asset work list. Work in the **consumer project's root**, not this skill's installation. The result is `plar.txt`: ordinary JSON with stable asset IDs, source bindings, consumer locations, requirements, destinations and next actions. It describes what is needed; PIXL's PX2 store retains production jobs, candidates and acceptance evidence.

## Understand and allocate

Read the project's instructions and available source overview/index/MOC, then verify its pointers against the relevant entry points. If no useful overview exists, retain a focused map of the consumers and backend transitions you actually inspect. If it already has `plar.txt`, read the queue and refresh affected rows. Use CodeGraph first when the project has a `.codegraph/` index; otherwise use the host's code tools. Follow actual UI/renderer consumers through imports, manifests, loaders and backend state transitions. Group shared visual roles into one asset with multiple consumers. A function without an image does not automatically need one.

Inspect existing art and the visible UI when available. Distinguish missing files, placeholders, reusable assets, visual mismatches and intentionally procedural/text-only elements. Note dynamic paths or unavailable modules in coverage.unresolved. Scope claims to the code and runtime actually inspected; a filename search is not exhaustive coverage.

For each visual role, connect:
- Purpose and visible states to file/symbol/usage locations.
- Applicable canvas/frame geometry, projection, reference style, edge/alpha policy, timing, pivots, tile rules and import behavior to their sources.
- The output destination, checks at the actual display size, dependencies, unresolved choices and one concrete next action.

Preserve explicit requirements, observations, proposals and unknowns separately. Use only relevant properties; do not invent a palette, alpha ban or resolution to fill a template. Record user instructions in a small project brief file when they are not already addressable. References convey style; measurements of them do not automatically become rejection rules. When visual input is required, add source-bound references with an explicit role (style, identity, pose, layout, palette, mask or motion) and instructions stating what to preserve.

## Save and use

Read [the format and operations](references/format.md) when creating or editing the work list. `pixl_plar_save` validates the supplied document, binds new local sources and retains previous versions using an expected hash. `pixl_plar_read` returns queue summaries; pass `asset_id` for the complete selected row and its source/dependency context. Focused reads also return transitive dependency requirements/issues, actual source hashes, absolute project paths, visual references and a derived production view with pending jobs and acceptance state. Use that view to choose resumption versus new preparation; an editable status label is not production evidence. Pass the requirements_hash to a delegate; it changes with relevant requirements or source bytes, not unrelated queue progress. The portable CLI provides the same operations. Ordinary file editing is also supported; re-read and validate afterward.

For refresh, read the queue before editing. Its changes report identifies drift and transitive dependents; after a save, or with `plar read --since PRIOR_HASH`, it compares authored requirements against retained history. operations remain available when their broader scope is needed.

a repository-wide inventory. Neither route turns a sample into approved production.
# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

## Caller: inspect before adopting

Open the packet and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:

1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.

For each criterion that can reject a candidate, retain a short caller-side comparison: criterion ID, the exact relevant source wording/locator (or explicit expert-choice basis), what the criterion adds or omits, and the finding. Group genuinely identical rules, but cover every rejection rule; a global "all restrictions come from the brief" claim is not this comparison. If a derived rule is stricter than the source, consider a source-conforming result it would reject before adopting it.

Keep process requirements, output requirements and diagnostic proxies distinct. A required production route is checked through actual calls and downloaded-byte provenance; a property of the resulting image is evidence only when it establishes that claim. Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.

Save a concise `caller-review.json` (or equivalent named fields) with reviewer role, reviewed packet hash, `consistent` / `changes_requested` / `needs_input`, per-criterion comparisons and other findings tied to request locations and source evidence, and the next action. `consistent` means the planned contract matches this assignment; it is not provider execution or asset acceptance.

If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.

If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.

## Carry the comparison through production

Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.

The final caller opens the delivered assets, checks the actual request and output against this contract, and records its own observations. Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. For a rejected candidate, retain the failure and the revised request/criteria; changing a checker merely to pass the candidate is a contract change, not an asset correction.
# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.
# Provider submission and recovery operation

Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.

Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.

## Required context

- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.

Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.

## Prepare a saved request

Prefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging. Preserve image transport identifiers with their local source hashes. The optional HTTP route below is a selected integration, not a substitute for every MCP workflow.

When the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`
to inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.
It currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,
not live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.
`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task
and output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;
do not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once
(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`
decodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation
requires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.
Unknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.
Mocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.

1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Capture observation time from the host clock when observing/recording the response (for example, Python datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()); keep provider event time separate. Do not invent a precise time from the session date, and omit optional timestamps that were not observed. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.

Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.

## Claim once, then call the actual provider

Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.

The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.

Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.

If submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.

For delegated work, compare the saved prepared request with the exact arguments in the [reviewed request packet](request-review.md) before dispatch. Changed arguments or criteria require an updated comparison; an unchanged reviewed contract does not require the user to repeat authorization.

## Resume and reconcile

Start with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.

A resource ID belongs to the connection that returned it. Use that same provider/account context for lookup or retrieval; never carry a simulated or unrelated provider ID into a real service. If the originating connection cannot return an image, retain that limitation and its observed state. Separate future production uses its own actual request and provider identity under the assignment; it is not retrieval of the simulated job. A finished request-only assignment does not terminate its queued job: before another request for the same asset, resolve the pending attempt with supported originating-connection evidence, or keep a truly separate assignment/context explicit. Changing task/output IDs within the asset store cannot bypass its pending attempt.

| Saved state / issue | Next operation |
|---|---|
| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |
| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |
| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented loo

Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.
139	
140	Save a concise `caller-review.json` (or equivalent named fields) with reviewer role, reviewed packet hash, `consistent` / `changes_requested` / `needs_input`, per-criterion comparisons and other findings tied to request locations and source evidence, and the next action. `consistent` means the planned contract matches this assignment; it is not provider execution or asset acceptance.
141	
142	If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.
143	
144	If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.
145	
146	## Carry the comparison through production
147	
148	Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.
149	
150	The final caller opens the delivered assets, checks the actual request and output against this contract, and records its own observations. Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. For a rejected candidate, retain the failure and the revised request/criteria; changing a checker merely to pass the candidate is a contract change, not an asset correction.
151	# Agent-to-agent asset work
152	
153	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
154	
155	## Caller → specialist
156	
157	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
158	
159	| Context | What the specialist needs |
160	| --- | --- |
161	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
162	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
163	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
164	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
165	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
166	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
167	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
168	
169	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
170	
171	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
172	
173	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
174	
175	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
176	
177	## Specialist → caller while working
178	
179	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
180	
181	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
182	
183	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
184	
185	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
186	
187	## Specialist → caller at completion
188	
189	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):
190	
191	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
192	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
193	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
194	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
195	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
196	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
197	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
198	
199	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
200	
201	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
202	
203	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
204	
205	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
206	
207	Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.
208	# Provider submission and recovery operation
209	
210	Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.
211	
212	Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.
213	
214	## Required context
215	
216	- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
217	- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
218	- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
219	- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.
220	
221	Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.
222	
223	## Prepare a saved request
224	
225	Prefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging. Preserve image transport identifiers with their local source hashes. The optional HTTP route below is a selected integration, not a substitute for every MCP workflow.
226	
227	When the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`
228	to inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.
229	It currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,
230	not live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.
231	`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task
232	and output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;
233	do not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once
234	(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`
235	decodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation
236	requires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.
237	Unknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.
238	Mocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.
239	
240	1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
241	2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
242	3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Capture observation time from the host clock when observing/recording the response (for example, Python datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()); keep provider event time separate. Do not invent a precise time from the session date, and omit optional timestamps that were not observed. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
243	4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.
244	
245	Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.
246	
247	## Claim once, then call the actual provider
248	
249	Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.
250	
251	The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.
252	
253	Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.
254	
255	If submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.
256	
257	For delegated work, compare the saved prepared request with the exact arguments in the [reviewed request packet](request-review.md) before dispatch. Changed arguments or criteria require an updated comparison; an unchanged reviewed contract does not require the user to repeat authorization.
258	
259	## Resume and reconcile
260	
261	Start with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.
262	
263	A resource ID belongs to the connection that returned it. Use that same provider/account context for lookup or retrieval; never carry a simulated or unrelated provider ID into a real service. If the originating connection cannot return an image, retain that limitation and its observed state. Separate future production uses its own actual request and provider identity under the assignment; it is not retrieval of the simulated job. A finished request-only assignment does not terminate its queued job: before another request for the same asset, resolve the pending attempt with supported originating-connection evidence, or keep a truly separate assignment/context explicit. Changing task/output IDs within the asset store cannot bypass its pending attempt.
264	
265	| Saved state / issue | Next operation |
266	|---|---|
267	| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |
268	| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |
269	| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented lookup/status capabilities and retained evidence; do not dispatch or recreate |
270	| Submitted/running with ID | Inspect that exact resource using its discovered status tool, then record the observed response |
271	| Succeeded | Retrieve the actual output through the host, import local candidate bytes, then evaluate acceptance |
272	| Failed | Preserve failure, establish its consequence and any still-valid retry authorization, then use a new job ID for a new attempt |
273	| Legacy unjournaled job | Inspect its actual available history manually; do not attach a fictional journal or ignore pending work |
274	| File/hash error | Preserve the diagnostic and restore the exact retained bytes from available history/backups before continuing; do not rewrite receipts to make a changed file pass |
275	
276	A crash between claim and host submission also leaves unknown. If no provider lookup can resolve whether the request was sent, leave that uncertainty explicit and continue independent work. Elapsed time cannot authorize a retry. A confirmed non-acceptance or terminal failure may support a failed observation and a newly authorized attempt; record that evidence first. Automatic remote exactly-once delivery is not claimed.
277	
278	On `stale_write` or `store_locked`, no dispatch grant was returned. Reread the state and owner information, then reconcile the attempted local change. Do not blindly repeat job-dispatch if another writer already claimed it. Immutable blobs left by a failed publication are unreferenced preparation data; state.px is the publication authority.
279	
280	## Import and hand back to acceptance
281	
282	Download with the actual host/provider mechanism into the project. Then run `job-import STORE JOB OUTPUT CANDIDATE DOWNLOADED_PATH EVIDENCE_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`. DOWNLOADED_PATH is relative to ROOT. This copies a byte snapshot into the store and creates X.of for the original F, plus a retained import event and J.xs reference. It preserves the downloaded original. It does not nominate the candidate, measure the image, grant V, or finish T.
283	
284	Import rejects changed output/contract/criterion context. Keep the returned file and original history; reconcile the intended plan explicitly before associating it. A new interpretation must not relabel an old generation as though it used the new contract. Submitted observations can still be recorded while the plan has drifted.
285	
286	Retrieve the imported X to obtain its retained path/hash. Run relevant mechanical inspection, review the actual image at native and enlarged scale, and exercise the required destination checks. Follow the [intake/sample acceptance procedure](intake-sample.md) to nominate a candidate deliberately and record each Q's pass, fail or unavailable verdict. Provider success and journal-retention receipts cannot satisfy those requirements.
287	
288	The operation stops with a truthful recovery action or an imported candidate ready for its specified acceptance checks. Handoff includes the job and candidate IDs, actual observed state, retained paths, unresolved checks and the next dependency. No finished asset family or engine readiness follows from this local operation alone.
289
